He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State Buckeyes]]. ==Early life and high school career== Branham was raised in [[Columbus, Ohio]]. Starting in 5th grade, he trained under Jason Dawson in Columbus.{{Cite web|url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2021/07/123564/chasing-perfection-how-malaki-branham-went-from-a-gangly-fifth-grader-to-an-ohio-state-freshman?amp|first=Colin|last=Hass-Hill|title=CHASING PERFECTION: HOW MALAKI BRANHAM WENT FROM A GANGLY FIFTH-GRADER TO HERALDED OHIO STATE FRESHMAN|website=Eleven Warriors}} He moved to [[Akron, Ohio]] to go to high school at [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting/2020/07/115271/qa-coach-st-vincent-st-mary-dru-joyce-explains-what-malaki-branham-brings-to-ohio-state?amp|first=Colin|last=Hass-Hill|title=Q&A: ST. VINCENT-ST. MARY COACH DRU JOYCE EXPLAINS WHAT MALAKI BRANHAM BRINGS TO OHIO STATE|website=Eleven Warriors}} At St. Vincent-St. Mary, he won two state championships in 2018 and 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://ohiostatebuckeyes.com/roster/malaki-branham/|title=Malaki Branham Bio|website=Ohio State Athletics}} He was named first team All-Ohio in his junior and senior seasons.{{Cite web|url=https://ohsaaweb.blob.core.windows.net/files/Sports/Basketball-Boys/2019-20/2020OPSWAAll-OhioBoysBKBTeams.pdf|title=2020 OPSWA All-Ohio Boys Teams|website=OHSAA.org}}{{Cite web|url=https://ohsaaweb.blob.core.windows.net/files/Sports/Basketball-Boys/2020-21/BoysBasketballAll-OhioTeam2021.pdf|title=All-Ohio Boys Teams|website=OHSAA.org}} As a senior, Branham averaged 21.3 points, 5.1 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.8 steals per game. In his senior season, he was named [[Ohio Mr. Basketball]]{{Cite web|url=https://www.ohsaa.org/Sports/News/malaki-branham-named-ohio-mr-basketball|title=Malaki Branham Named Ohio Mr. Basketball|website=OHSAA.org}} and made the [[Jordan Brand Classic]], which was not played for to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/ohiostate/.amp/recruiting/ohio-state-basketball-recruiting-2021-guard-signee-malaki-branham-named-to-jordan-brand-classic|first=Andrew|last=Lind|title=2021 Ohio State Basketball Signee Malaki Branham Named To Jordan Brand Classic|website=Buckeyes Now FN}} ===Recruiting=== Branham was a consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and ranked as the best player in Ohio. On July 22, 2020, Branham committed to playing college basketball for [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] over offers from teams such as [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]], and [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{Cite BRANHAM CONTINUES TO LOOK LIKE TRUE SECOND OPTION FOR OHIO STATE AMID IMPRESSIVE THREE-GAME RUN|website=Eleven Warriors}} He scored a career-high 35 points in a 87–79 overtime win against [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] after a nearly month-long COVID pause.{{Cite web|url=https://amp.dispatch.com/amp/9075525002|first=Adam|last=Jardy|title=Ohio State's Malaki Branham enjoys 'Welcome to Star City' in Nebraska|website=The Columbus Dispatch}} In a three-game stretch in February, he scored 22, 27, and 31 points.{{Cite web|url=https://scarletandgame.com/2022/02/25/ohio-state-basketball-fans-nervous-malaki-branham/amp/|first=Ryan|last=Stano|title=Ohio State basketball fans nervous about Malaki Branham|website=ScarletAndGame.com}} As a freshman, he averaged 13.7 points, 3.6 rebounds and two assists per game. Branham was named [[Big Ten Conference|Big Ten]] Freshman of the Year as well as Third Team All-Big Ten.{{cite press release|url=https://bigten.org/news/2022/3/8/2021-22-big-ten-mens-basketball-postseason-honors-announced.aspx|title=2021-22 Big Ten Men’s Basketball Postseason Honors Announced|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]] |date=March 8, 2022 |accessdate=March 8, 2022}} On April 1, 2022, Branham declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{Cite web |date=2022-04-01 |title=Ohio St.'s Branham enters draft, but may return |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33647890/ohio-state-freshman-malaki-branham-entering-nba-draft-leaves-door-open-return |access-date=2022-04-01 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} He later signed with an [[sports agent|agent]], forgoing his remaining eligibility.{{cite web |last=Jardy |first=Adam |title=2022 NBA draft: Ohio State's Malaki Branham says goodbye to Buckeyes |url=https://amp.dispatch.com/amp/9549272002 |website=[[The Columbus Dispatch]] |access-date=April 29, 2022 |date=April 27, 2022}} He is a potential lottery pick in the draft. ==Career
